title: Order Response
description: A message a consumer (e.g. Computyme) sends back about an order it previously received. This is an event/delta: it reports what changed, it does not re-assert the whole order. Every response references the canonical orderId your platform owns, so the loop closes without guessing. Transport-agnostic: the same JSON applies whether delivered by file drop or API/webhook.

schemaVersion.description: Response contract version. Independent of the order contract version.

responseType.description: Selects which optional block carries the detail: acknowledgement, fulfillment, status, or exception.

orderRef.description: Which order this response is about. orderId is YOUR canonical id; consumerOrderId is the consumer's own id for round-tripping.

orderId.description: The canonical order id from the original order contract (metadata.orderId). Authoritative key.

orderNumber.description: Human-facing order number, echoed for convenience.

consumerOrderId.description: The consumer's internal id for this order (e.g. Computyme's CT-99821). Lets you store the mapping.

respondedAt.description: When the consumer generated this response.

messageId.description: Unique id for THIS response message, for idempotency and de-duplication. Strongly recommended.

acknowledgement.description: Present when responseType is ACKNOWLEDGEMENT. Computyme returns this immediately on receipt of an order, as a single terminal answer: ACCEPTED means the order is valid and will be processed; REJECTED means it kicked out and will NOT be processed. Every order receives exactly one acknowledgement — silence is not acknowledgement.

ackResult.description: ACCEPTED = valid, will be processed. ACCEPTED_WITH_CHANGES = will be processed but with flagged deviations. REJECTED = kicked out, will not be processed.

rejectReason.description: Required when ackResult is REJECTED; omit otherwise. Machine code for why the order kicked out.

message.description: Human-readable detail. REQUIRED when ackResult is REJECTED (so the kickout can be acted on) and recommended for ACCEPTED_WITH_CHANGES.

fulfillment.description: Present when responseType is FULFILLMENT_UPDATE. Reports shipment and per-line outcomes.

fulfillmentGroupId.description: Which fulfillment group from the original order this update concerns. Null if order-wide.

shipments.description: Shipments executed by the consumer. Mirrors the order contract's shipment shape so both sides speak the same language.

lineId.description: The lineId from the original order's items[]. This is how lines are matched back.

freightCost.description: Actual freight cost for this shipment, if reported.

lines.description: Per-line outcome. Use to report backorders, short-ships, and cancellations against the original lineIds.

lineId.description: Matches items[].lineId in the original order.

statusUpdate.description: Present when responseType is STATUS_UPDATE. A coarse status the consumer wants to report (e.g. invoiced, closed).

status.description: Reuses the canonical order status vocabulary so both sides agree on meaning.

exceptions.description: Present when responseType is EXCEPTION (or attached to any response). Problems the consumer hit while processing.

code.description: Stable machine code for the problem, if the consumer has one.

references.description: Cross-system identifiers keyed by system name, same convention as the order contract.

extensions.description: Namespaced consumer-specific data. Read only your own namespace. Adding here never requires a schema change.
